p1.explanation: A 'virtual power plant' sounds invented, but the BPU approved one on Nov 12: smart thermostats, EV chargers and home batteries cut power use at peak hours, and their owners get paid for it.
p1.con_line_false_alarm: Real. 'Virtual power plant' sounds like my work, but the BPU got there first.

p2.tell: The axis starts at 19¢, and the bars compare April 2025, before the summer spike, with July 2026, 15 months later. July to July, prices rose 0.3%.
p2.explanation: Real EIA numbers, framed to mislead. A cropped axis makes a 26.5% gap look like a cliff, and cherry-picked months turn an old jump into a 'one year' rise. Prices did jump in 2025. Over the past year they've been nearly flat.
p2.con_line_fooled: Real numbers, honest-looking bars. I just picked where they start.
p2.con_line_caught: Fine. You checked the data. I'll crop it better next time.

p3.tell: He said 'no NET increase.' Some charges go up and others go down: Atlantic City Electric's bill rises $4.09 and falls $4.14.
p3.explanation: One deleted word changes the promise. 'No net increase' means increases are offset by cuts elsewhere, not that nothing goes up. The crop also drops the start of the sentence, which ties it to items voted on earlier that month.
p3.con_line_fooled: Three letters: n, e, t. That's all I took.
p3.con_line_caught: You found the 'net.' I'll have to cut bigger words.

diff.shown: …these actions will result in no increase in electricity rates.
diff.original: Taken together with the items on the agenda earlier this month, these actions will result in no net increase in electricity rates and a slight decrease in gas rates.
removed: Taken together with the items on the agenda earlier this month,
and a slight decrease in gas rates

p4.explanation: Startling, but true: it's straight from the BPU's own press release. Bills jumped in 2025, which is the rise the doctored chart smuggled into its 'one year' window.
p4.con_line_false_alarm: Surprising isn't the same as fake. A grain of salt, not the whole shaker.

p5.explanation: Real and word for word, from New Jersey Monitor's coverage of the Nov 12 BPU vote. Peak hours drive prices, which is why the board is paying people to use less power then.
p5.con_line_false_alarm: Real. Not everything that sounds dramatic is a trick.
